introduction_markdown: Multiple choice paper (0510 Biology 1, June 2021, Ordinary Level, General Certificate of Education Board). Duration: one and a half hours. Answer ALL 50 questions; all questions carry equal marks. Each question has four suggested answers A, B, C and D; mark only one answer for each question. Non-programmable calculators are allowed.
enonce_intro_markdown: **Multiple choice questions** - choose the one correct answer, A, B, C or D. Section I (questions 1-7): independent questions. Section II (questions 8-20): biological diagrams. Section III (questions 21-25): one or more responses correct. Section IV (questions 26-30): pairs of statements. Section V (questions 31-40): lettered headings and a description. Section VI (questions 41-50): biological situations.

Section through a flower with labels Q (anther), R (stigma) and S (ovary) (Question 10).
Carbon cycle: CO2 in atmosphere, Animals, Plants, Fossils; the arrow from Fossils to atmospheric CO2 is labelled X (Question 11).
Female reproductive system with structures numbered 1 to 5; 3 is the ovary (Question 14).
Potted plant enclosed in a transparent polythene bag in sunlight, with condensed liquid on the inside of the bag (Question 41).

questions.enonce_markdown:
*SECTION I - directions as printed, summarised:* Each of these questions or incomplete statements is followed by four suggested answers. Select the best answer in each case and mark the answer sheet appropriately.

Is a characteristic of birds;
questions.corrige_markdown: Birds have a crop (food storage) and a gizzard (muscular grinding organ that replaces teeth) as part of the digestive system. Gills belong to fish, scales for body protection to reptiles and fish, and birds are homoiothermic (warm-blooded), not poikilothermic. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: possess crop and gizzard as digestive features.
presence of scales on body for protection.

questions.enonce_markdown: Light energy is converted to chemical energy during photosynthesis and stored in the form of;
questions.corrige_markdown: In photosynthesis light energy is trapped by chlorophyll and stored as chemical energy in carbohydrates (glucose, then starch). Minerals, vitamins and water do not store this energy. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Healthy carriers of HIV are,
questions.corrige_markdown: A healthy carrier has the virus in the body but shows no symptoms; such a person can still pass the virus on through blood, sexual contact or from mother to child. Option B is wrong because carriers are infectious, and option D describes a person already sick with AIDS. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: HIV negative people who look sick.
people who look healthy, have the virus but cannot infect others.
people who look healthy, have the virus and can infect others.
people who have reached the AIDS stage.

questions.enonce_markdown: The function of the swim bladder in fish is to;
questions.corrige_markdown: The swim bladder is a gas-filled sac. By adding or removing gas the fish changes its buoyancy and so controls the depth at which it floats or swims. Fast swimming is done by the tail and fins, and vibrations are detected by the lateral line. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: prevent the fish from changing its direction.
control the depth at which fish swims.
enables the fish to detect vibrations.

questions.enonce_markdown: Which three elements make up carbohydrates?
questions.corrige_markdown: Carbohydrates (sugars, starch, cellulose) contain only carbon, hydrogen and oxygen, with hydrogen and oxygen in the ratio 2:1 as in water. Nitrogen is an extra element of proteins. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following is an excretory process?
questions.corrige_markdown: Excretion is the removal of metabolic waste products made inside the cells. Carbon dioxide, produced by respiration, is excreted by the lungs. Insulin and saliva are secretions, and faeces (undigested food) are egested, not excreted. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: Release of insulin from the pancreas.
Release of saliva from the salivary gland.
Removal of carbon dioxide from the lungs.
Removal of feaces from the alimentary canal.

questions.enonce_markdown: If the solute percentage inside the cell is 65% while the solute percentage outside the cell is 35%. In what direction will water move?
questions.corrige_markdown: Water moves by osmosis from the region of higher water potential (the dilute solution, 35% solute outside) to the region of lower water potential (the concentrated solution, 65% solute inside), through the partially permeable cell membrane. So water moves into the cell. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: Moves in and out of cell.
No movement in and out of cell.

questions.enonce_markdown:
*SECTION II - directions as printed, summarised:* This group of questions relates to biological diagrams. Select the best answer for each question.

The diagram below shows the human forearm

![fig-1](gce-ol-biology-2021-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_1.png)

What happens to the muscles X and Y when the arm is flexed?

*Options as printed:* A) X: Relaxes, elongates; Y: contracts, shortens   B) X: Contracts, elongates; Y: relaxes, shortens   C) X: Contracts, shortens; Y: relaxes, elongates   D) X: Relaxes, shortens; Y: contracts, elongates
questions.corrige_markdown:
Muscle X lies on the front (inner side) of the upper arm, in the angle formed when the forearm bends: it is the biceps (flexor). Muscle Y lies on the back of the upper arm: it is the triceps (extensor). Muscles work in antagonistic pairs. When the arm is flexed the biceps (X) contracts and shortens, pulling the forearm up, while the triceps (Y) relaxes and elongates. A muscle cannot contract and elongate at the same time, so option B is impossible, and options A and D describe extension of the arm or impossible combinations.

**Intended answer: C (X: Contracts, shortens; Y: relaxes, elongates).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: Trace the correct path of impulse transmission.
questions.corrige_markdown: In a neurone the impulse is received by the dendrites, passes along the dendron to the cell body, then along the axon to the nerve endings and on to the effector. The order is therefore dendrite, dendron, axon, effector. **Answer: A.**

In the diagram Q is an anther (it carries the pollen), R is the stigma (the receptive top of the carpel) and S is the ovary. Self-pollination is the transfer of pollen from the anther to the stigma of the same flower, that is from Q to R. Pollen does not go to the ovary (S) directly; it germinates on the stigma. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
The diagram below represents the circulation of carbon in nature.

![fig-3](gce-ol-biology-2021-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_3.png)

What biological process is represented by X?
questions.corrige_markdown: In the carbon cycle carbon dioxide is returned to the atmosphere by respiration of animals and plants, but the arrow marked X starts from fossils (coal, oil, gas) and ends at atmospheric carbon dioxide. Burning fossil fuels is combustion, which releases the stored carbon as carbon dioxide. Photosynthesis would remove carbon dioxide from the air, and death does not release carbon dioxide directly from fossils. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify the structure that prevents reflux of blood from the aorta to the left ventricle.
questions.corrige_markdown: At the base of the aorta are semilunar (pocket-shaped) valves. They close when the ventricle relaxes and so stop blood flowing back from the aorta into the left ventricle. The bicuspid valve lies between the left atrium and left ventricle and the tricuspid valve between the right atrium and right ventricle. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Choose the correct site of reabsorption of glucose and amino acids in the kidney nephron.
questions.corrige_markdown: Ultrafiltration takes place in the Bowman's capsule. All the glucose and amino acids (and much of the water and salts) are then reabsorbed back into the blood in the proximal convoluted tubule by active transport. The loop of Henle reabsorbs mainly water and salts, and the distal convoluted tubule adjusts salts and water. **Answer: D.**

Structure 3 is the ovary (1 is the uterus, 2 the oviduct, 4 the cervix and 5 the vagina). The ovary secretes the sex hormones oestrogen and progesterone. FSH and LH are secreted by the pituitary gland, not by the ovary. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The image formed on the retina from an external object is;
questions.corrige_markdown: The cornea and lens act as a convex lens system. The image on the retina is real (it can be received on a screen), smaller than the object and upside down (inverted); the brain interprets it the right way up. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: In which part of the gut does the chemical digestion of proteins begin?
questions.corrige_markdown: The enzyme pepsin, working in the acid medium of the stomach, begins the digestion of proteins into peptides. The mouth digests only starch (amylase); the duodenum and ileum continue protein digestion with trypsin and other enzymes, but do not begin it. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: In genetic engineering, cut DNA pieces are joined using?
questions.corrige_markdown: DNA ligase is the enzyme that joins (seals) the cut DNA fragments, for example a gene and a plasmid. The restriction enzyme is the one that cuts DNA. DNA polymerase copies DNA and helicase unwinds the double helix. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Below are four listed organisms.

1 Carnivore

2 Decomposer

3 Herbivore

4 Producer

In an ecosystem, in which order does energy flow through these organisms?
questions.corrige_markdown: Energy enters the ecosystem through the producer (4, green plants), passes to the herbivore (3) that eats the plants, then to the carnivore (1) that eats the herbivore, and finally the decomposer (2) obtains energy from dead remains of all of them. The order is 4, 3, 1, 2. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: In which part of the female reproductive system does implantation occur?
questions.corrige_markdown: After fertilisation in the oviduct, the zygote divides into an embryo (blastocyst) which travels to the uterus and sinks into its thick, spongy lining. This is implantation. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which vessel returns oxygenated blood to the heart?
questions.corrige_markdown: The pulmonary vein carries oxygenated blood from the lungs to the left atrium. The vena cava returns deoxygenated blood from the body, the pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood to the lungs, and the aorta carries oxygenated blood away from the heart. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
*SECTION III - directions as printed, summarised:* For each of the questions below, ONE or MORE of the responses is (are) correct. Decide which of the responses is (are) correct, then choose: A if 1, 2 and 3 are correct; B if 1 and 2 only are correct; C if 2 and 3 only are correct; D if 1 only is correct.

During over heating of the body;

1 the hairs of the skin stand erect.

2 the blood vessels below the skin dilate.

3 there is increased production of sweat.
questions.corrige_markdown: When the body overheats, the hairs lie flat (they stand erect to trap air when it is cold, so statement 1 is false). The skin arterioles dilate (vasodilation) so more blood flows near the surface and loses heat, and the sweat glands produce more sweat, which cools the body as it evaporates. Statements 2 and 3 are correct. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Typical of mammals.

1 Have mammary glands.

2 Have sweat glands.

3 Are homodonts.
questions.corrige_markdown: Mammals feed their young on milk from mammary glands (1) and have sweat glands in the skin (2). They are heterodonts (teeth of different kinds: incisors, canines, premolars, molars), so statement 3 is false; homodont (all teeth alike) describes reptiles and fish. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
After fertilization has taken place in a flowering plant;

1 the corolla and calyx wither and fall off.

2 the ovary gradually ripens into a seed.

3 the ovule becomes the fruit.
questions.corrige_markdown: After fertilisation the petals (corolla) and sepals (calyx) wither and fall off (1 is correct). The ovary develops into the fruit and the ovule develops into the seed, so statements 2 and 3 are each the wrong way round. Only statement 1 is correct. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
The malaria parasite;

1 destroys nerve cells.

2 destroys red blood cells.

3 causes anaemia.
questions.corrige_markdown: Plasmodium multiplies inside the red blood cells and bursts them (2). The loss of red blood cells leads to anaemia (3). It does not attack nerve cells (1 is false). **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Auxins;

1 are produced at the shoot tips.

2 increase growth in shoot.

3 inhibits growth in roots.
questions.corrige_markdown: Auxins are plant growth hormones made at the tips of shoots (1). In a shoot they stimulate cell elongation and so increase growth (2), while in roots the same hormone, at the concentrations present, inhibits elongation (3). All three statements are correct. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
*SECTION IV - directions as printed, summarised:* Each question consists of a statement in the left-hand column followed by a second statement in the right-hand column. Decide whether the first is true or false and whether the second is true or false, then choose: A if both are true and the second is a correct explanation of the first; B if both are true but the second is NOT a correct explanation of the first; C if the first is true but the second false; D if the first is false but the second true.

**First statement:** Insulin increases blood sugar level while glucagon decreases it.

**Second statement:** Insulin and glucagon are antagonistic hormones.
questions.corrige_markdown: The first statement is false: insulin LOWERS blood sugar (it makes the liver convert glucose to glycogen) while glucagon RAISES it. The second statement is true because the two hormones have opposite effects (they are antagonistic). **Answer: D.**

choix.texte: True, True: the 2nd statement is a correct explanation of the first.
True, True: the 2nd statement is NOT a correct explanation of the first.

questions.enonce_markdown:
**First statement:** Lack of vitamin D causes rickets.

**Second statement:** Vitamin D promotes the absorption of calcium salts for bone formation.
questions.corrige_markdown: Both statements are true. Vitamin D helps the intestine absorb calcium (and phosphate) for building bones, so without it the bones stay soft and bend, which is rickets. The second statement therefore explains the first. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: True, True: the 2nd statement is a correct explanation of the first.
True, True: the 2nd statement is NOT a correct explanation of the first.

questions.enonce_markdown:
**First statement:** The biotic factors in an ecosystem include temperature and water.

**Second statement:** Ecosystems are made up of both abiotic and biotic factors.
questions.corrige_markdown: The first statement is false: temperature and water are abiotic (non-living) factors; biotic factors are living things such as plants, animals and microbes. The second statement is true. **Answer: D.**

choix.texte: True, True: the 2nd statement is a correct explanation of the first.
True, True: the 2nd statement is NOT a correct explanation of the first.

questions.enonce_markdown:
**First statement:** Mosquitoes transmit the malaria causing parasite.

**Second statement:** Malaria is contracted from drinking standing water.
questions.corrige_markdown: The first statement is true: the female Anopheles mosquito transmits Plasmodium when it bites. The second statement is false: malaria is contracted through the mosquito bite, not by drinking water (standing water only serves as a breeding place for mosquitoes). **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: True, True: the 2nd statement is a correct explanation of the first.
True, True: the 2nd statement is NOT a correct explanation of the first.

questions.enonce_markdown:
**First statement:** Maize plants interspersed with leguminous plants grow healthier.

**Second statement:** Leguminous plants increase the nitrogen content of the soil.
questions.corrige_markdown: Both statements are true. Leguminous plants have root nodules containing nitrogen-fixing bacteria (Rhizobium) which enrich the soil with nitrates; the maize growing between them uses this nitrogen and grows healthier. The second statement explains the first. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: True, True: the 2nd statement is a correct explanation of the first.
True, True: the 2nd statement is NOT a correct explanation of the first.

questions.enonce_markdown:
*SECTION V - directions as printed, summarised:* Each question consists of four lettered headings A, B, C, D. Select the heading which is closely related to the description which follows.

Results from meiotic division.
questions.corrige_markdown: Meiosis produces gametes (sex cells) with half the number of chromosomes; of the cells listed only the sperm cell is a product of meiosis. Nerve, blood and muscle cells are body cells formed by mitosis. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Pressure receptor.
questions.corrige_markdown: The Pacinian corpuscle, deep in the skin, responds to strong pressure. The hair plexus detects light touch of hairs, free nerve endings detect pain, and Meissner's corpuscle detects light touch. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Allow movement of bones in one direction only.
questions.corrige_markdown: A hinge joint (elbow, knee) allows movement in one plane only, like a door hinge: bending and straightening. A ball and socket joint moves in all directions, a pivot joint rotates, and a gliding joint slides in several directions over a flat surface. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Small circular pieces of DNA found in certain bacteria.
questions.corrige_markdown: Plasmids are small circular DNA molecules found in the cytoplasm of bacteria, apart from the main chromosome, and used as vectors in genetic engineering. Recombinant DNA is DNA made by joining pieces from different sources, a restriction enzyme cuts DNA and a clone is a group of identical organisms or cells. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A chemical that can be used to absorb oxygen in an experiment.
questions.corrige_markdown: Alkaline pyrogallic acid (pyrogallol) absorbs oxygen. Sodium hydroxide and potassium hydroxide absorb carbon dioxide, and sodium bicarbonate gives off or buffers carbon dioxide. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Prevents wearing out of bones at joints.
questions.corrige_markdown: The ends of the bones at a joint are covered with smooth cartilage, which cushions them and stops the bone surfaces from wearing away as they rub. A ligament joins bone to bone, a tendon joins muscle to bone, and synovial fluid lubricates the joint (it reduces friction but the cartilage is the protective layer). **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Undergoes complete metamorphosis.
questions.corrige_markdown: Complete metamorphosis has four stages: egg, larva, pupa and adult. The honey bee goes through all of them. The cockroach, grasshopper and termite have incomplete metamorphosis (egg, nymph, adult) with no pupa. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A food stuff that remains brown when iodine is dropped on it.
questions.corrige_markdown: Iodine solution is brown-orange and turns blue-black only if starch is present. Cassava, cooked rice and plantain are rich in starch and turn blue-black. In a ripe banana most of the starch has been changed to sugar, so the iodine stays brown. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Using a cat to eliminate rats at home.
questions.corrige_markdown: Using a natural predator (the cat) to reduce the population of a pest (rats) is biological control. Pesticides are chemical control; competition and scavenging are not pest-control methods. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: It's a characteristic of white blood cells.
questions.corrige_markdown: White blood cells have a nucleus and no haemoglobin (the pigment is in red cells), they defend the body, and they live only a short time. Red blood cells have no nucleus, carry out transport and live about 120 days. So the characteristic of white blood cells is that they lack haemoglobin. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
*SECTION VI - directions as printed, summarised:* This group of questions deals with biological situations. Each situation is followed by a question. Select the best answer for each question.

When the set up below was exposed to the sun for one hour, gas bubbles condensed into liquid on the inside of the polythene bag.

![fig-5](gce-ol-biology-2021-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_5.png)

Identify the condensed liquid and its origin.
questions.corrige_markdown: In the sun the leaves lose water vapour by transpiration. The vapour cools against the inside of the transparent polythene bag and condenses into drops of liquid water. Oxygen and carbon dioxide are gases and do not condense at these temperatures. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: Carbon dioxide from respiring soil microbes.

questions.enonce_markdown: In an experiment using guinea pigs to verify the functions of parts of the brain, one structure was removed and it was observed that the animal could not move properly and had no balance at all. Which structure was removed?
questions.corrige_markdown: The cerebellum coordinates muscular movement and controls balance and posture; without it the animal cannot move properly. The medulla controls involuntary actions (breathing, heartbeat), the cerebrum controls thought and voluntary action, and the pituitary is an endocrine gland. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Two students were asked to breathe out into two conical flasks containing clear liquids. David breathed into conical flask K and the liquid remained clear. Nadia breathed into conical flask L and the liquid in it turned milky. Identify the contents of the flask K and L and the gas that caused the change in L.

| | Flask K | Flask L | Gas |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | Distilled water | Lime water | O$_2$ |
| B | Lime water | Caustic soda | O$_2$ |
| C | Pyrogallic acid | Caustic soda | CO$_2$ |
| D | Caustic soda | Lime water | CO$_2$ |
questions.corrige_markdown: Exhaled air contains carbon dioxide, which turns lime water milky (calcium carbonate). So flask L, which turned milky, contained lime water and the gas was CO$_2$. In flask K the liquid stayed clear because caustic soda (sodium hydroxide) absorbs carbon dioxide without turning milky. Option A names oxygen, which does not turn lime water milky, and B and C put caustic soda or pyrogallic acid in the flask that turned milky. **Answer: D.**

choix.texte: Flask K: Distilled water; Flask L: Lime water; Gas: O$_2$
Flask K: Lime water; Flask L: Caustic soda; Gas: O$_2$
Flask K: Pyrogallic acid; Flask L: Caustic soda; Gas: CO$_2$
Flask K: Caustic soda; Flask L: Lime water; Gas: CO$_2$

questions.enonce_markdown: In an experiment to demonstrate that mammals give off carbon dioxide during respiration, 3 flasks and a respiratory bottle labeled A, B, C and D are used. Flask A contains a chemical to absorb CO$_2$ from incoming air, Flask B contains lime water which should stay clear, Flask C is the respiratory bottle which contains the small mammal to respire and Flask D contains lime water to test the gas produced. What modification will you make in C if the mammal were to be replaced by a green plant?
questions.corrige_markdown: A green plant in the light photosynthesises and uses up the carbon dioxide it produces, so the lime water in D would stay clear. To show that the plant gives off carbon dioxide in respiration, photosynthesis must be stopped by keeping the plant in the dark, i.e. covering bottle C with a black cloth. A dish of sodium hydroxide would absorb the carbon dioxide, calcium hydroxide (lime water) would be turned milky by it, and a transparent bag would still let light in. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: Cover C with a black cloth.
Place a dish of calcium hydroxide in C.
Place a dish of sodium hydroxide in C.
Cover C with a transparent polythene bag.

questions.enonce_markdown: Each egg in a woman's ovary carries an X chromosome. For a normal male zygote to be formed during fertilization,
questions.corrige_markdown: A normal male has the sex chromosomes XY. The egg always gives an X, so the sperm must give a Y. A sperm carries only ONE sex chromosome (X or Y) after meiosis, so options C and D are impossible, and an X sperm would give a girl (XX). **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: A sperm carrying the X chromosome fuses with the egg.
A sperm carrying the Y chromosome fuses with egg.
A sperm carrying an XY chromosome fuses with the egg.
A sperm carrying an XX chromosome fuses with the egg.

questions.enonce_markdown: What chemical substance is tested for to show that photosynthesis has taken place in a leaf?
questions.corrige_markdown: The glucose made in photosynthesis is quickly changed to starch for storage in the leaf, and starch is easily detected with iodine solution (blue-black). So the leaf is tested for starch. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: In addition to availability of water, which other conditions are essential for seed germination?
questions.corrige_markdown: Germination needs water, oxygen (for aerobic respiration to release energy) and a suitable temperature (for enzyme activity). Light, carbon dioxide and soil are not required. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: In every ecosystem plants occupy the first trophic level. This is because, they;
questions.corrige_markdown: Plants (producers) trap solar energy by photosynthesis and convert it into chemical energy in food, which becomes available to all the other trophic levels. Being numerous, tolerant of weather or anchored by roots does not explain their place at the first level. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: are capable of converting solar energy.
have roots that anchor them into the soil.

questions.enonce_markdown:
The diagram below is a food chain.

Grass → grasshopper → praying mantis → toad.

Which organism in the food chain above is a secondary consumer?
questions.corrige_markdown: Grass is the producer, the grasshopper eats grass and is the primary consumer, the praying mantis eats the grasshopper and is the secondary consumer, and the toad is the tertiary consumer. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of these is a genetically engineered process?
questions.corrige_markdown: Human insulin is made by inserting the human insulin gene into a bacterium (using plasmids), which then makes the hormone: this is genetic engineering. Bread and wine making use yeast naturally (fermentation) and oil spills are cleaned with natural microbes, with no change to their genes. **Answer: A.**
